ރަނގަޅަށް ބައިބޯ، މިހާ ބައިބޯ ޖަމާޢަތެއް އެއް ޕާޓީއަކަށް އޮތް މަޖިލީހެއްގައި، ބައި މަދު އިދިކޮޅު ފަރާތަކަށް އިޙުތިރާމުކޮށް އެ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް އޯގާތެރިކޮށް ހިތި މަޖިލީހެއް ވެސް މިހާހިސާބަށް ގާއިމުވެފައެއް ނޯންނާނެ. ވަރަށް ގުޅިގެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މަސައްކަތްކުރެވޭތޯ ބަލަނީ. އެ ބޭފުޅުން ހަމަ މިތަނަށް އެއްޗެއް ބިލެއް، ރަނގަޅު އެއްޗެއް ހުށަހަޅައިފި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާ މިހާހިސާބަށް ރަނގަޅަށް ބަހުސްކޮށް އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި މަޖިލީހުން އޮންނާނީ ފާސްކޮށްދީފަ. ވަރަށް ތާކުންތާކުނުޖެހޭ މި ކަހަލަ ގަރާރެއް ވިއްޔާ އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ދެކޮޅަށް ކިރިޔާ ވެސް އެއްޗެއް މި ބުނެލަނީ. އެހެންނޫނީ ނުތެދުވެ މިތާ ވާހަކަނުދައްކާ ގިނަ ފަހަރަށް މި ތިބެނީ. ހަމަ މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ކުރާ އިޙުތިރާމެއްގެ ބޮޑުކަމުން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. މި ތިބީ 75 މެންބަރުންނާއި 12 މެންބަރުންނާ. އެހެންވީމާ، ވަރަށް ބަލައިގެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި މަޖިލީހުން
މަސައްކަތް މި ކުރަނީ. މިއިން ބޭފުޅަކަށް އުނދަގޫނުވާނެ ގޮތަށް ހުރިހާ ކަމެއް މި ކޮށްދެނީ. ކޮމިޓީތަކުގައި ވެސް މަޖިލީހުގެ ގަވާއިދުން ޖާގަ ލިބޭ މިންވަރަށްވުރެ ރަނގަޅަށް އޯގާތެރިކޮށް ހުންނާނީ މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ޖާގަދީފަ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ބައެއް ކޮމިޓީތަކުގެ ބޮޑެތި ކޮމިޓީތަކުން ޖާގަދޭންނުޖެހޭ ތަންތަނުގައި ވެސް ހުންނާނެ. އެއް ޖާގަ ދޭންޖެހޭ ތަންތަނަށް ދެ ޖާގަ ވެސް ދީފައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސަށް ރަނގަޅަށް އެނގިވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ މިކަން. އެހެންވީމާ، ވާހަކަ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް ވަރަށް ގިނައިން ވަރަށް ގިނަ ގޮތްގޮތަށް ދެއްކިދާނެ. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި ސަރުކާރަކީ ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި މަޝްރޫޢުގެ ނަން އެ ކިޔަނީ މަޝްރޫޢުތައް މި ތަފުސީލާ އެއްކޮށް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އެ ދެއްވީ. މިހާހިސާބަށް މި ސަރުކާރުން މަސައްކަތްކުރި ހިންގާ ނިންމި ޕްރޮޖެކްޓުތަކުގެ އަދަދު މިދިޔަ ސަރުކާރުތަކާ ނުބައްދަލު އަދަދަކަށް ރަނގަޅަށް ހުރީ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ފައިދާހުރި ގޮތުގައި މި މަޖިލީހުން މި ފާސްކުރެވުނު ގާނޫނުތަކާއި، ގާނޫނުތަކަށް ގެނެވުނު އިޞްލާޙުތަކަކީ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅަށް ބަލައިގަންނަ ގާނޫނުތަކާއި، އިޞްލާޙުތަކެއް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވައިލަން ބޭނުންވަނީ މި ސަރުކާރަކުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އެއްވެސް، އެއްވެސް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތެއްގެ މައްޗަށް ނިކަމެތިކަމެއް ލިބޭނެ އެއްވެސް ކަމެއް ނުކުރާނެ. ތެދުވެރިކަމާ އެކު، އިޚުލާސްތެރިކަމާ އެކު ވެރިކަންކުރާ ވެރިޔެއް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަކީ. ބަހަކުންނެއް ނޫން އިނގޭތޯ. ޢަމަލުން އެކަން ދައްކަނީ. ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން އެކަމަށް ހެކިވާނެ. މި ބޭފުޅުން ވަރަށް ފޯރިލާފައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ދައްކާ އެބަ ނިމިގެންދިޔަ ލޯކަލް ކައުންސިލު އިންތިޚާބުގެ ވާހަކަ. މިދިޔަ ލޯކަލް ކައުންސިލު އިންތިޚާބަކީ މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް އެނގިވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ މިހާހިސާބަށް 2008 އިން ފެށިގެން މި ގާއިމުކުރެވުނު ސަރުކާރުތަކަށް ބަލައިފި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާ އެއިރެއްގައި ގާއިމުވެފައި އޮތް ސަރުކާރަކަށް އެންމެ ގިނަ އަދަދެއްގެ ގޮނޑި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން ދިން ލޯކަލް ކައުންސިލު އިންތިޚާބަކީ މިދިޔަ އިންތިޚާބު. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަށް، ޕީ.އެން.ސީ.އަށް، މި ސަރުކާރަށް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން ތާއީދު ދިނީ. އޯކޭ، ސިޓީތަކުގައި ބައެއް ގޮނޑި އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް ނުލިބި ހިނގައްޖެ. އެހެންނަމަވެސް، ރާއްޖޭގައި ހުރި 186 ރަށަށް ބަލައިފި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާމު މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށްވުރެ 60 އަށްވުރެ ގިނަ ކައުންސިލަރުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިތުރޭ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ކޮބައިތޯ ނާކާމިޔާބޭ ދެންނެވެން އޮތް ސަބަބަކީ. ޑަބްލިއު.ޑީ.ސީއަށް ބެލިޔަސް ހަމަ އެގޮތަށް. އެހެންވީމާ، ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ކަންކަން މި ސަރުކާރުން މި ކުރަނީ، މި ކޮށްދެނީ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން ބޭނުންވާ ގޮތަށް. ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޝްވަރާއާއި އެ ބޭފުޅުންގެ ލަފަޔާއި އިރުޝާދުގެ ދަށުން. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަކީ އަބަދު ވެސް ރައްޔިތުންނާ ގާތުން މަސައްކަތްކުރޭ. މިހާރު އެދަނީ ވަން ޓު ވަން. ވަން ޓު ވަން. މި ދުވަހަކު ދިވެހި ވެރިޔަކު ކުރި ކަމެއްތޯ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؟ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއެއްގެ ފައިންޕުޅު ފެނުމަކީ މި ޤައުމުގައި ނާދިރު ކަމެއް މީގެ ކުރީގައި. ނާދިރު ކަމެއް. އެއީ މާވަހަރެއް ހޮވުން ކަހަލަ އެއް ކަމެއް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް.
އެހެންނަމަވެސް، މިދިޔަ 2 އަހަރާއި 3 އަހަރާ ގާތްވަމުން އަންނަ އިރު ދިވެހި ހުރިހާ، ރާއްޖޭގައި މީހުން ދިރިއުޅުއްވާ ހުރިހާ ރަށަކަށް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ދަތުރުކޮށް، ހުރިހާ ރައްޔިތުންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، ހުރިހާ ކައުންސިލުތަކާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، ހުރިހާ ޑަބްލިއު.ޑީ.ސީތަކާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، ހުރިހާ ރަށެއްގެ ކަމުވޮށިގެންވާ މީހުންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، މާލޭގެ ހުރިހާ އަވަށްތަކުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، މާލޭގެ ހުރިހާ ވިޔަފާރިވެރިންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް، ރާއްޖޭގެ ހުރިހާ ވިޔަފާރިވެރިންނާ ބައްދަލުކޮށް ހުރިހާ އެންމެންގެ މަޝްވަރާގެ މަތީން ހުރިހާ ކަމެއް ކުރަމުން މި ދަނީ. އަނެއްކާ އެ ފެއްޓެވީ މިހާރު ވަން ޓު ވަން. ކޮންމެ ރައްޔިތަކަށް ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއާ ބައްދަލުކުރެވޭނެ. ކޮންމެ ރައްޔިތަކަށް. ކޮންމެ ރައްޔިތަކު ބޭނުންވީމަ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވާ އެ ރައްޔިތަކު އެ އެދޭ ކަމަކީ އެ ކޮށްދެވެން އޮތް ރަނގަޅު ކަމެއް ކަމަށް ވަންޏާމު އެކަމަކަށް އިޖާބަދީ ޤައުމީ ލެވެލްގައި ވެސް، ފަރުދީ ލެވެލްގައި ވެސް، ރަށު ލެވެލްގައި ވެސް، ސިޓީ ލެވެލްގައި ވެސް ހުރިހާ ކަމެއް އެ ދަނީ ކޮށްދެމުން. މި ބޭފުޅުންނަކަށް ނުކޮށްދެވޭނެ. ރައީސުން ހޮވިދާނެ. ރާއްޖޭގެ ރައްޔިތަކަށް ނުފެންނާނެ އެއިން ރައީސަކު. މިދިޔަ އެއްވެސް ވެރިކަމެއްގައި ހޮވި އެއްވެސް ރައީސަކު ބައްލަވާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ހުރިހާ ކައުންސިލުތަކާ ރަށްރަށަށް ގޮސް އެ ކައުންސިލުތަކާއި ރައްޔިތުންނާ ބައްދަލުކުރި އެއްވެސް ވެރިޔެއް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ނޫނީ ނުހުންނާނެ. އެހެންވީމާ، މީގެ ކުރިން ވެރިންނަށް ނުކުރެވުނު، ނުކުރި ނުބައި ކަންތައްތައް، ރައްޔިތުން އެދޭ ކަންކަން ނުކުރީމަ، އެހެން ވެރިންނަށް ނުވީމަ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އެ ކަންކަން ކުރައްވާތީ ހަޖަމުނުވެގެން މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް. ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ވާހަކައެއް ދައްކާނެ އެއްވެސް ވާހަކައެއް ނުލިބޭ މި ބޭފުޅުންނަށް. ކުދިކުދި ބޮޑެތި ކަންކަން ނުފެނުނީމަ، ކުދިކުދި ކަންކަން ބޮޑެތިކުރަން މި ބޭފުޅުން މަސައްކަތްކުރަނީ. އެހެންނެއް ނުވާނެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ބޮޑެތި ކަންކަން ބޮޑެތިކުރެވޭނީ. ކުދި ކަންކަން ބޮޑެއްޗެއް ނުކުރެވޭނެ. މީހަކު ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކޮށްފިއޭ. މަގެއްގައި ކާރެއް އެބަ އޮތޭ. ރަށަކަށް ދޯންޏެއް ފުރައިގެން ހިނގައްޖޭ. ނޫނިއްޔާ ކުކުޅެއް ބިއްސައަޅައިފިއޭ. މިކަހަލަ މީކީ ވެރިކަމަކާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ދެކޮޅަށް ދައްކާ ސައިޒުގެ ވާހަކައެއް ނޫން ދެއްތޯ ރައީސް. އެހެންވީމާ، ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވައިލަން ބޭނުންވަނީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި މަޖިލީހުގައި ވެސް މަސައްކަތް ހުރިއްޔާ މި އަންނަނީ ބޮޑު ޗުއްޓީއެއް. މަސައްކަތް ހުރި ކަމަށް ވަންޏާ ހަމަ ޗުއްޓީ އެއްކޮށް ރައީސް މަސައްކަތުގައި އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ތިބޭނަން އިރާދަކުރެއްވިއްޔާ. ހަމަ އެއްކޮށް. ދޮޅު މަހުގެ ޗުއްޓީއެއް ކުރިއަށް އޮތީ، ފެންނަން އޮތީ. އެ ދޮޅު މަސްދުވަސް ހަމަ ދުއްވައިލާނީ މަސައްކަތް އޮތިއްޔާ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ މިތާ ތިބި 12 މެންބަރުންނަށް މި ދަންނަވަނީ، މަސައްކަތް އޮތިއްޔާ މާލޭގައި ހަމަ ތިބޭނީ މި މަޖިލީހުގައި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް، ޤައުމަށް، ސަރުކާރަށް ފަހިވާ ގޮތަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމުގައި ދެމިތިބޭނީ. ނުދާނަން ޗުއްޓީއަކަށް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު ނިންމައިލަމުން ދަންނަވާނީ މި ކަހަލަ ގަރާރުތައް މި މުހިންމު މަސައްކަތްތައް މި މަޖިލީހުގައި ކުރަން ހުރިއިރުގައި ހުށަނޭޅުމަކީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ވަރަށް ބޮޑު އެދުމެކޭ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ދެ ޕާޓީގެ ވެސް މި ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ
މެންބަރުންނަކީ ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި، ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ވަރަށް ދެރަވެފައި މި ދޭތެރެއިން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ތިބީ. އެއީ މިތާ ތިބީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ މި 12 މެންބަރުންނާ ދޭތެރޭގައި ވަރަށް އިހާނެތިކޮށް މިދިޔަ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގެ މިދިޔަ ޕްރައިމަރީއާއި އެތެރޭ އިންތިޚާބުތަކުގައި ކަންވެގެންދިޔައީ. އެއީ މިސާލަކަށް މިތާ 12 ތިބޭރުގައި މިހާރު ކޮންމެ ދުވަހަކު މި ފެންނަނީ 3 ނުވަތަ 2. ޕީ.ޖީ ލީޑަރެއް ނުފެނޭ. ޑެޕިއުޓީ ޕީ.ޖީ ލީޑަރެއް ނުފެނޭ. ދެން ހުންނަ ބޭފުޅެއް ނުފެނޭ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަކަށް ނޭނގެ މި ކަންކަންވަނީ ކިހިނެއް ކަމެއް އެއްގޮތަކަށް ވެސް. ގަރާރު ހުށަހެޅި މިތާ ވާހަކަދައްކަވައިފި. އެއީ ދެތެއް. ގަރާރު ހުށަހެޅި މެންބަރު ފުރަތަމަ އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި ދޭ ތަފުސީލާއި އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މި ދައްކާ ވާހަކަ އަޑުއަހާފައި މިއަށް ޖަވާބު ދެއްވަންޖެހޭނެ ދެއްތޯ އެންމެ ކުޑަމިނުން. އޭރަށް ދެއްތޯ މިތާ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެނގޭނީ ގަރާރެއް މި ތަނަށް އެއްލައިލާފައި މެންބަރު ދޮރުން ފިލާ ރައްކާވީމަ ކޯއްޗަކަށް ވާނީ. ދެން ޑެޕިއުޓީ ލީޑަރު އެ ބުނަނީ ތިމަންނަ ކަންނޭނގެއޭ. ތިމަންނައާ މަޝްވަރާކޮށްފައި ހުށަހެޅި އެއްޗެއް ނޫނޭ މިއީކީ. އެހެންވީމާ، އެގޮތަށް ކަންކަން ނުކުރަން ނަސޭހަތްތެރިވަމުން އަޅުގަނޑު ވާހަކަކޮޅު ނިންމައިލާނީ. ދެއްވި ފުރުޞަތަށް ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރު ދަންނަވަން. ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރިއްޔާ ރައީސް.
speeches.en:
Thank you, Honourable Speaker. Yes! What we are debating in this Majlis now today is a resolution submitted by the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, accusing the government of dismissing a very large number of employees from various companies, in order to see how the members of this honourable Majlis view that matter. Honourable Speaker, in particular, from the NDP side, the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency and the Honourable Member for North Mahchangolhi constituency submit these resolutions very often. Generally, the resolutions that come from Mahchangolhi have some good qualities. However, I regret to say that I cannot believe that what comes from Kendhoo constituency are resolutions that even the people of that constituency would be very satisfied with. Honourable Speaker, as we speak on this resolution, it is a great misconception for the MDP members to think that the Maldivian people will have forgotten how, in the past MDP governments, they treated Maldivian citizens, particularly employees working in companies, and particularly citizens in the opposition who disagreed with their ideas. Honourable Speaker, many of those who spoke on this resolution just now have noted that when the MDP submits a resolution with such importance, what this resolution states is a very big claim. This accuses this government of unjustly dismissing people in various government jobs in government companies, ministries and other places too, and of dismissing a very large number of people and leaving them destitute. But, as some Honourable Members noted, when such an important resolution was submitted, when such a resolution was sent to this Majlis after so much thought and over so many days, to some extent names, for example, Inamadhoo / Miruskge, Ahmed Shakir. Kendhoo / Husnuheenaage, Mohamed Abubakuru. If names like this had been in this resolution, saying these are the people, these are the numbers, this many were dismissed, if it had disclosed this to the people to some degree together with names, I think the public's interest in it might have been greater. Honourable Speaker, in both of the times the MDP came to power, in its first government too, the ruler himself, the President, said directly at the podium in front of the people that he would show the sword to those who do not belong to the MDP. That they would treat those who do not support the MDP and MDP members in a vastly different way. And that is exactly how they acted. That is indeed a true statement. Look, the uninhabited islands in the Maldives on which expensive resorts are built, to make resorts, without any price

were distributed to their people when they came to power in 2008, during the MDP government. Without any price. Uninhabited islands that are given for 4, 5 million dollars, islands given to build resorts, were distributed without any price to the people demonstrating on the streets for them and others there. Fortunately, when power fell from the hands of some of them, those uninhabited islands were lost. Islands had even been given to people who could not even afford to travel to the island where it lay. Such things happened in our atoll too. In that government an island was given to two or three people. However, when islands were given to people who could not afford to leave Malé, travel there, land on the island and look at it, because it costs money, the islands were lost, they did not know how to sell them, and those too slipped from their hands, fortunately. That is the state things were in under the MDP then, Honourable Speaker. Then we need to consider, Honourable Speaker, that the Maldivian state is in reality not as wealthy and prosperous a state as we think. If we look at President Maumoon's government, the state budget then, Honourable Speaker, was approximately 4 billion, 6 billion, 5 billion. I recall that in 2008, when he stepped down from power, the state budget then was also about nine or ten billion rufiyaa. Now the state budget has gone past 50 billion, Honourable Speaker. We citizens also need to look at how much revenue the state receives. While we pass budgets of 57 billion or budgets of 50 billion in the People's Majlis and spend and serve the people, what the state receives as revenue, Honourable Speaker, is 35 billion, 34 billion rufiyaa a year. Therefore, every year the state budget has a deficit, Honourable Speaker; it goes into debt by 15 or 12 billion rufiyaa. Going on like that, the state's debt today has risen to 160, 180 billion rufiyaa. Therefore, Honourable Speaker, this is something to think about. These matters are considered by leaders who love the Maldivian nation and love the Maldivian people. Today's President is an exemplary leader of that kind. Since this government has not printed money, they are now saying it printed money by taking out some 2.5 billion rufiyaa from the pension fund. If that is so, Honourable Speaker, then when people's money kept in savings in banks is taken and used, that money is being printed too. Printing money; necessarily taking something kept in savings somewhere and using it cannot be regarded as printing money, Honourable Speaker. The Honourable Speaker is also a very strong businessman. For example, the Honourable Speaker may also have, in the name of the company Redwave, at Bank of

Maldives, 1 billion rufiyaa in a savings account kept for 5 years. That 1 billion rufiyaa, for example, Bank of Maldives or the other banks also use for lending and such; the money those wealthy people keep in those banks for a long term. So when loans are given from that money, that money is being printed too, isn't it. Therefore, misleading the Maldivian people by calling it printing money or something else, such things, Honourable Speaker, are things the Maldivian people will think about very well today. In the 3rd year, the 2nd year, the government is now going into its 3rd year. Has this Majlis passed a supplementary budget even once? No. In every past government, the MDP would empty the budget passed for that year before the middle of the year, then send another supplementary budget to this Majlis, pass it and spend more money. Therefore, however, what the Maldivian people need to consider is that in reality, from 2018 to 2023 in the MDP government, they from jobs in their government, in their first government, Honourable Speaker, I have also made a note, in the MDP government they obtained in 2008; that lasted about 2 years. Within those 2 years, 330 people were dismissed from jobs at various government companies and elsewhere on the grounds that they belonged to other parties. 330 employees. 330. I am stating the number, Honourable Speaker. When the MDP government ended in 2018, 421 people had been unjustly dismissed from their jobs. 421 people. As this government approaches 3 years, Honourable Speaker, there will not be even 15 people; not a single person will have been unjustly dismissed from a job by this government. Not one person. All those the MDP dismissed in its 2 governments were employees dismissed because they did not belong to them, did not support the MDP, and did not bow their heads to them. What I am stating is hundreds; one time 330. In the second government, 421 people dismissed from jobs. But when these people submitted a resolution to this Majlis and debated it, when they spoke, they could not at the very least include in that resolution whether this government dismissed 100 people, 20 people, 15 people or 10 people. Therefore, it does not become the MDP to talk about this, Honourable Speaker. Regarding jobs, the first thing to consider is who encouraged Maldivian citizens to come to work in government companies, government SOEs, ministries and such places. Why that encouragement, or why the people wanted it. Every time these people come to power, they bankrupt all the small-sized companies in the Maldives. All the companies. Dr. Shamheed and his colleagues will know this very well.

That is, these are strong people who work by forming companies. These are people who do mosques, housing and such things. These people, these people too will know the state that companies of that size were in in the Maldives during the MDP's 2 governments. Honourable Speaker, when we concluded the government, when this MDP government ended, how many owners of how many companies were standing in front of Fenaka Corporation holding placards because they could not pay their employees' salaries, with 4 billion rufiyaa left unpaid to various companies in the MDP government. Fenaka Corporation alone had 4 billion rufiyaa unpaid. All the work had been commissioned on credit. All the work was commissioned on credit. All the work done, if it was done on an island in the Maldives, every pipe and cable laid underground for development needs to be dug up again, Honourable Speaker. From the day the government ended, they have needed to be removed. No work, no development work on top of it can be done except by removing and fixing what these people did underground for development. A road can be tarred only after fixing the water if these people laid water, and fixing the sewerage if they laid sewerage. All that work was done using materials unsuitable for doing those things. Dr. Shamheed and his colleagues will know these things, Honourable Speaker. These people did things with companies that make pipes. There are cables and such in the Maldives, electricity cables produced on uninhabited islands under the name of a cable factory. Whatever way that was done, we are not talking about whether these people are capable or not capable. We are not saying useless things, Honourable Speaker. This is the true story. What I see is my constituency, Honourable Speaker. There are 5 islands in my constituency. In those 5 islands, water systems were established in some islands during their government. When their government ended, in some islands the water systems were left in the hope of getting power [unclear]. In every island where they were left, joints are being made every 4 feet, 5 feet. All the pipes have sunk at the bottom, Honourable Speaker. How can we tar a road there without first fixing that system. That is everything that was done. Not a single good thing was done under the ground [unclear]. Therefore, I say that in reality, if it is something done in an unseen place, the MDP will do it badly. I am not talking about doing something good in a visible place. Therefore, for the MDP in reality; then there is the matter of this Majlis. Dr. Shamheed and his colleagues tweet, don't they, saying there is no work in this People's Majlis. First, if one is a member of the People's Majlis, that member should look at how people's parliaments operate in other countries of the world. The People's

Majlis is not a place where you come at 9 o'clock every day and then work until 6 in the evening, Honourable Speaker. The People's Majlis is a body established to make the laws needed by the government of the time, to amend those laws, to make a new law if one needs to be made, and to put right anything that is going badly in that government. The People's Majlis is a place for making laws and amending laws. Therefore, the people, in this Majlis we need to look at the past 19th People's Majlis and the current 20th People's Majlis; this too has been said on many days, Honourable Speaker. When these 2 Majlises reached 2 and a half years, or 2 full years, if we look at the work rate of the two Majlises, we need to look at which Majlis got more work done, Honourable Speaker. Can't these people check? If they write a letter to the administrative desk asking to look at the work done, the work carried out, the work done by this Majlis, they will provide in writing the amount of work done, with details. Earlier, because of how much these people talked about it, some days ago we looked at how the work done in the 2 Majlises stood by this point. When we looked then, about twenty more bills' worth of work had been done in this Majlis, Honourable Speaker. Compared to the 19th Majlis, the work done by this Majlis in that period was about twenty bills more. In this Majlis, in every recess, during half of every recess, when there was work, we have done that work. These people do not need to tweet saying that this Majlis is not working and talk about it not working. There has never been a People's Majlis in the Maldives that has passed bills and laws better, more carefully, and more important and beneficial to the people and the country than this one has by this point. The MDP members here will acknowledge this. In a Majlis where one party has such a good majority, such a supermajority, no Majlis will have existed until now that treated the small minority opposition with such respect and care. We try to work very closely together. If they submit a bill here, something good, we will have debated it well and passed it in this Majlis by now. Only when it is a nonsensical resolution like this do we say even a little something against it. Otherwise, most of the time we sit here without standing up to speak. Purely out of the great respect we have for these people, Honourable Speaker. There are 75 members and 12 members here. Therefore, we do our work in this Majlis very carefully.

That is how we work. Everything is done so that none of them face any difficulty. In committees too, they will have been given space more generously than the Majlis regulations allow. You will find places, in some of the big committees, where we did not have to give them space, and still did. In places where one seat had to be given, two have been given, Honourable Speaker. The Honourable Speaker knows this well. Therefore, we could talk a great deal, in many ways. Therefore, this government of ours is in reality called by the name of projects; our Honourable President has given those projects with details. The number of projects this government has carried out and completed by now is incomparably better than past governments, Honourable Speaker. The laws passed by this Majlis in ways beneficial to the people, and the amendments made to laws, are laws and amendments the Maldivian people accept very well, Honourable Speaker. Therefore, what I want to say is that our Honourable President will not do anything from this government that would bring hardship to any, any Maldivian citizen. Our Honourable President is a leader who governs with honesty and sincerity. Not in words, you know. He shows it in deeds. The Maldivian people will bear witness to that. These people, very excitedly, Honourable Speaker, talk about the local council election just concluded. These people will know that the last local council election, if we look at the governments established since 2008 up to now, was the local council election in which the Maldivian people gave the most seats to the government in place at the time. The Maldivian people gave their support to our Honourable President, to the PNC, to this government. Okay, in the cities we did not get some seats. However, if we look at the 186 islands in the Maldives, we have more than 60 more councillors than they do, Honourable Speaker. What reason is there to call it a failure. The same if you look at the WDCs. Therefore, in reality, what this government does, what it does for people, is done the way the Maldivian people want. Under the consultation, advice and guidance of the Maldivian people. Our Honourable President always works close to the people. Now he is doing one to one. One to one. Is this something a Maldivian leader has ever done, Honourable Speaker? Seeing the feet of a President was a rare thing in this country before. A rare thing. It was something like finding ambergris, Honourable Speaker.

However, over the past 2 years, approaching 3 years, our Honourable President has travelled to every inhabited island in the Maldives, met all the people, met all the councils, met all the WDCs, met the prominent people of every island, met the people of all the wards of Malé, met all the businesspeople of Malé, met all the businesspeople of the Maldives, and is doing everything on the basis of everyone's consultation. And now he has started one to one. Every citizen can meet the President. Every citizen. Whenever a citizen wants, he meets them, and if what that citizen requests is a good thing that can be done, he responds to it, and everything is being done at national level, individual level, island level and city level. These people cannot do that. They may elect presidents. The citizens of the Maldives will not see a president among them. Of any president elected in any past government, look, there will be no leader other than our Honourable President who went to all the councils and islands of the Maldives and met those councils and the people. Therefore, the bad things that past leaders could not do or did not do, when they did not do what the people wanted, when other leaders could not, because our Honourable President does those things, these people cannot digest it. In reality these people cannot find anything at all to talk about. When they find no big issues, these people try to make small things big. It will not be like that, Honourable Speaker. Only big things can be made big. Small things cannot be made into something big. Someone has been dismissed from a job. There is a car on a road. A boat has left for an island. Or a hen has laid an egg. These are not the size of things to talk about against a government, are they, Speaker? Therefore, in reality, what I want to say is that we too in this Majlis, if there is work, a long recess is coming. If there is work, we will be at work throughout the recess, Speaker, God willing. All of it. A two-month recess lies ahead, as we see. We will fly through those two months if there is work; I say this to the 12 MDP members here: if there is work, we will stay right here in Malé and remain working in this Majlis in ways that benefit the people, the country and the government. I will not go on recess, Honourable Speaker. Therefore, in concluding, I say that it is our great request that such resolutions not be submitted while such important work is to be done in this Majlis. We, the members of this People's Majlis from both parties,

are in reality, in reality, very saddened by what is going on in between. That is, regarding our 12 members here, things went very disgracefully in the past MDP primary and internal elections. That is, for example, of the 12 here, every day now we see 3 or 2. No PG leader is seen. No deputy PG leader is seen. No one else is seen. We do not know at all how these things are. The member who submitted the resolution spoke here. That is all. The member who submitted the resolution should at the very least first listen to the details we give and what we say and respond to it, shouldn't he. Only then would the people here know what becomes of it when a resolution is thrown in here and the member slips out the door and hides. Then the deputy leader says he doesn't know. That this was not something submitted after consulting him. Therefore, I conclude my remarks advising against doing things that way. I thank you very much for the opportunity. Thank you very much, Speaker.

speeches.name: Ahmed Saleem
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: އާދެ! ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު. އަޅުގަނޑު ހަމަ އެއްޗެއް ދަންނަވައިލާނަން މި މަޖިލީހުގެ މަސައްކަތާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން. މިއީ 20 ވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލިސް. މިހާރު ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް 100 އަހަރާ ދިމާއަށް މި ދަތުރުކުރަނީ. މަޖިލީހުގައި ރާއްޖެއަށް ބޭނުންވާ މައިގަނޑު ގާނޫނުތައް އެހެރީ ހަދައި ނިމިފަ. ދެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް އަލަށް ނުކުންނަ ގާނޫނެއް އާ ކަމެއްގައި ހެދިދާނެ. ދެން މަޖިލީހުގެ ގާނޫނަކަށް ގެންނަންޖެހޭ އިޞްލާޙެއް އެ ކަހަލަ ކަމެއް ގެނެވިދާނެ. ދެން އެހެންވީމާ، މި ކަހަލަ ގޮތަކަށް މަސައްކަތް ހުރީ. އެހެންވީމާ، ކޮންމެ ދުވަހަކު އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް މަޖިލީހަށް ސަރުކާރުން ބިލުތަކެއް ފޮނުވުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތެއް ނޯންނާނެ. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް އަނެއްކާ ދަންނަވައިލަން ހަމަ އިދިކޮޅު ފަރާތްތަކަށް ވެސް، ޚާއްސަކޮށް އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ވެސް ހަމަ އަމިއްލައަށް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ކޮންމެ މެންބަރަކަށް ވެސް ބިލުތައް ހުށަހެޅުމުގެ ބާރު މެންބަރުންނަށް އޮވޭ. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ވިސްނަންޖެހޭނެ 100 އަހަރު މި ގާތްވަނީ ގާނޫނު ހަދާތާ. ދެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ކޮންމެ ދުވަހަކު ހަދާނެ ގާނޫނުތަކެއް ނޯންނާނެ އިނގޭތޯ. އެހެންވީމާ، އެކަން އަޅުގަނޑު ހަމަ ސާފުކޮށްލަން. އެއީ މިކަމާ ބެހޭގޮތުން ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް އިންޓަރވިއުދީ، ބައެއް ނޫސްތަކުގައި ޖަހާ މި ކަހަލަ ކަންތައް ކުރާތީ އަޅުގަނޑު މިކަން ސާފުކޮށްލަދިނީ. ދެން އަޅުގަނޑު ފުރުޞަތު މި އަރުވަނީ ތުޅާދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޢަބްދުލްޙަންނާން އަބޫބަކުރަށް.
speeches.en: Yes! Thank you, Honourable Member. I will just say something about the work of this Majlis. This is the 20th People's Majlis. We are now heading towards about 100 years. The main laws the Maldives needs have been made in the Majlis. Then we may make a law that newly comes up, on some new matter. Then an amendment that needs to be brought to a law of the Majlis, that kind of thing may be brought. So the work is of this kind. Therefore, there will not be an opportunity every day for the government to send bills to us in the Majlis. Therefore, I would again like to say to the opposition parties too, and especially to the MDP too, that every Honourable Member has the power to submit bills on their own. Therefore, we must bear in mind that it is approaching 100 years since laws began to be made. And there will not be laws for us to make every day, you know. So I just want to clarify that. I clarified this because of things like giving many interviews about this matter and publishing it in some newspapers. Next I give the floor to the Honourable Member for Thulhaadhoo constituency, Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru.

speeches.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
speeches.heading: ތުޅާދޫ ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު ޢަބްދުލްޙަންނާން އަބޫބަކުރު ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އާދެ! ހުށަހެޅިފައިވާ ގަރާރަކީ ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު މަޢުރޫފް ޛާކިރު ހުށަހަޅުއްވާފައިވާ ގަރާރެއް. އާދެ! މި ގަރާރުގައި މި ބުނަނީ ސަރުކާރުގެ ކުންފުނިތަކުގެ ޚަރަދު ކުޑަކުރުމާއި މުވައްޒަފުންގެ އަދަދު އެކަށީގެންވާ މިންވަރުގައި ހިފެހެއްޓުމަށް ޓަކައި މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރުން ނިވާފަތްގަނޑެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހަދާ ވާހަކަ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވާނީ ކަނޑައެޅިގެން މިއީ ދޮގު ބުހުތާން ވާހަކައެއް. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ޚާއްސަކޮށް ފެނަކަ ކޯޕަރޭޝަނުން ހިނގަމުންގެންދިޔަ އިންޖީނުގެތައް އަދި ހަމަ ޚާއްސަގޮތެއްގައި އަޅުގަނޑު ފާހަގަކޮށްލާނަން ބ.އަތޮޅު އަޅުގަނޑު ދާއިރާގައި މިހިރަ އިންޖީނުގެތައް ސްޓެލްކޯއާ ހަވާލުކުރުމަށް ޓަކައި މި ކަންކަން ހިނގައި މި ދަނީ ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅަށް ކަމަށް. މިހެން މި ދަންނަވަން ޖެހެނީ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ކޮންމެ ކުންފުންޏަކީ ވެސް ވަކި ޝަޚުސެއް އިނގޭތޯ. އެގޮތުން ކޮންމެ ކުންފުންޏެއްގައި ވެސް ބޯޑެއް އެބަ އޮތް. އެ ބޯޑުން އެ ނިންމާ ގޮތަކަށް މެނުވީ އެ ކުންފުނީގެ ކަންތައްތައް ކުރިއަކަށް ނުގެންދެވޭ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ މި ސަރުކާރުން މުވައްޒަފުން މަދުކުރަންޖެހޭ ކަމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ވެސް ގަބޫލުކުރަން. އެކަމަކު އެ މަދުކުރުން މަދުކުރެވޭއިރުގައި ވަރަށް ގިނަ ގޮތްގޮތަށް މިކަން ސަރުކާރުގެ މި ދެންނެވި ފެނަކައިގެ ކުންފުނިން ބައްލަވާފައިވާ ކަމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ގަބޫލުކުރަން. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ކަމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހުރިހާ މުވައްޒަފުންނަށް އިނގޭތޯ، އަޅުގަނޑުގެ ދާއިރާގެ ހަމަ ހުރިހާ މުވައްޒަފުންނަށް ތިން މަހުގެ މުސާރައާއި އެލަވަންސާ އެކު ވަކިވުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތު ފެނަކައިން ދެއްވި. އެކަމަށް ޓަކައި ބައެއް މުވައްޒަފުން އެކަމަށް އިޖާބަ ވެސް ދެއްވި. ހަމަ އެގޮތަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ބަލައިލާއިރުގައި ސްޓެލްކޯއިން މި މުވައްޒަފުން އިނގޭތޯ، އަޅުގަނޑުގެ ދާއިރާގެ ގާތްގަނޑަކަށް 139 މުވައްޒަފުން ފެނަކައިގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރަމުން ދޭ. އެއީ ފެނާއި ނަރުދަމާގެ ކަންތަކުގައި އިނގޭތޯ، އަދި ކަރަންޓު. 139 މުވައްޒަފުންގެ ތެރެއިން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް މި ފެނުނީ އެންމެ ތިން މުވައްޒަފުން ވަކިކުރިތަން. ވަރަށް ގިނަ މުވައްޒަފުން ކެނޑިއްޖެތާ. ބެއްލެވިޔަސް މިކަން ވާނީ ޙަޤީޤަތަށް. އަޅުގަނޑު ސާފުކޮށްލިން އަސްލު މި ތިން މުވައްޒަފުންގެ މައްސަލައަކީ ކޮބައިތޯ. އަޅުގަނޑު ސާފުކޮށްލިއިރުގައި މި ތިން މުވައްޒަފުންގެ މައްސަލައަކަށްވަނީ އިންޓަރވިއުއިން ފެއިލްވެފައިވަނީ. މި ނޫން އެއްވެސް މައްސަލައެއް ޖެހިފައި އޮތް ކަމަކަށް އަޅުގަނޑަކަށް ގަބޫލެއް ވެސް ނުކުރެވޭ އަދި ސާފެއް ވެސް ނުވޭ. އަދި މިހާރު މި މުވައްޒަފުންތައް މި ދަނީ ސްޓެލްކޯގައި މަސައްކަތް ވެސް ކުރަމުން. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވާނީ އަސްލުގައި މި ކަހަލަ ގަރާރުތައް، ބޭގަރާރު ގަރާރުތައް ހުށަހަޅައިގެން؛ އަޅުގަނޑު މި ދަންނަވަނީ އަޅުގަނޑުގެ ދާއިރާގެ ވާހަކަ އިނގޭތޯ. އަޅުގަނޑުގެ ދާއިރާއިން މިކަން މި ކޮށްފައިވަނީ ހަމަ ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅަށޭ އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވައިލާނީ. އެހެންވީމާ، މިއީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ދާއިރައަށް ލިބުނު ހަމަ ވަރަށް ބޮޑު ކުރިއެރުމެއްކަން އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަވާނީ ފެނަކަ މި ފަދަ ހާލަތުގައި އޮއްވާ ސްޓެލްކޯ ފަދަ ރަނގަޅު ވަރުގަދަ ކުންފުންޏަކާ މިކަން ހަވާލުކުރެއްވީތީ އިނގޭތޯ. އަޅުގަނޑު ހަމަ މި ދެއްވި ފުރުޞަތަށް ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރުދަންނަވަމުން ވަކިވެލަން. ُ السَّالَم َ و ْ عَلَيْكُم.
speeches.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Thank you, Honourable Speaker. Yes! The resolution submitted is a resolution submitted by the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir. Yes! What this resolution says is that staff reductions, made to cut the expenditure of government companies and keep staff numbers at a reasonable level, are being used as a cover. Honourable Speaker, I say that this is definitely a false slander. Honourable Speaker, in particular the powerhouses that were run by Fenaka Corporation, and I will note in particular the powerhouses here in my constituency in B. Atoll, are being handed over to STELCO, and these things are going very well. I have to say this, Honourable Speaker. Every company is a separate legal person, you know. Accordingly, every company has a board. That company's affairs cannot proceed except in the way that board decides. Honourable Speaker, I too accept that this government needs to reduce staff. But I believe that when that reduction is made, the government's company, the Fenaka I mentioned, has looked at this matter in many ways. Honourable Speaker, first of all, Fenaka gave all the employees, you know, absolutely all the employees of my constituency, the opportunity to leave with three months' salary and allowances. Some employees accepted that. Likewise, when I look at these employees at STELCO, you know, about 139 employees of my constituency are working at Fenaka. That is in water and sewerage, you know, and electricity. Of the 139 employees, what we saw was only three employees being dismissed. As if a great many employees had been cut. Even if you look, this is how it really is. I checked what the issue with these three employees actually was. When I checked, the issue with these three employees was that they had failed the interview. I neither believe nor see any other issue having arisen. And these employees are now also working at STELCO. Therefore, I say that actually, by submitting such resolutions, baseless resolutions; I am talking about my constituency, you know. I would say that in my constituency this has been done very well indeed. Therefore, I say this is a very great advancement for our constituency, that while Fenaka is in such a situation, this has been handed over to a good, strong company like STELCO, you know. Thanking you very much for this opportunity, I take my leave. Peace be upon you.

speeches.name: Ahmed Saleem
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު. ދެން އަޅުގަނޑު ފުރުޞަތު މި އަރުވަނީ ހުޅުދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު މުޙައްމަދު ޝާހިދަށް.
speeches.en: Thank you, Honourable Member. Next, I give the floor to the Honourable Member for Hulhudhoo constituency, Mohamed Shahid.

speeches.name: Mohamed Shahid
speeches.heading: ހުޅުދޫ ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު މުޙައްމަދު ޝާހިދު ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ކެންދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު މަޢުރޫފް ޛާކިރު ހުށަހެޅުއްވި މި ގަރާރަށް ވާހަކަދައްކަން އަޅުގަނޑު ވެސް ފުރުޞަތަކަށް މި އެދުނީ މީގެ ކުރީގައި މި މަޖިލީހުގައި އެންމެފަހުން ކުރިއަށްދިޔަ ސެޝަނުގައި އެ ބޭފުޅުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވީ އަދި މިއަދު ވެސް އާންމުކޮށް އެ ދައްކަވަނީ ވަޒީފާއަށް މި ސަރުކާރުން މީހުން އައްޔަނުކުރާ ވާހަކަ. ރަށްރަށުގައި ތިބި ރައްޔިތުން ގިނަ އަދަދަކަށް ވަޒީފާތަކަށް އައްޔަނުކުރާ ވާހަކަ. މިއަދު އަނެއްކާ މި ހުށހެޅިގެން ކުރިއަށް މި ދަނީ ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރާ ވާހަކަ. އެހެންވީމާ، ފުރަތަމަ ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑު ގަބޫލުކުރަން އެބަ ޖެހޭ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ މި އައީއަކީ އަލަކަށް ނޫން މި ޤައުމަށް. މި ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާ މުޚާޠަބުކޮށް ވާހަކަދައްކައި ވެރިކަން ހޯދުމަށް ޓަކައި މަސައްކަތް މި ކުރަނީ އަލަކަށް ނޫން. ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަކަށް މި ކަމެއް ނޯޅޭނެ. އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއޭ ބުނީމަ ރައްޔިތުން މިހާރު ބިރުގަންނާނެ. ފަހަތަށް ދުއްވައިގަންނާނެ. އެއީ އެ މީހުން ދެއްކި ވާހަކައަކީ ވެރިކަމަށް އަންނަން އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ވެސް، 2008 ވަނަ އަހަރު ވެރިކަމާ ހަވާލުވެ ކަންތައް ކުރެއްވީ ކިހިނެއްތޯ؟ ޑޮލަރުގެ ވާހަކަ ވެސް އެބަ ދެކެވޭ. އޭރު ޑޮލަރުގެ އަގު ކިހާވަރެއްގައިތޯ ހުރީ؟ އެ ވެރިކަމުގައި ރައީސް ނަޝީދުގެ ދެ އަހަރާއި ބައިގެ ވެރިކަން ނިމިގެންދިޔަ އިރުގައި ޑޮލަރު ހުރީ ކިހާ ހިސާބެއްގައިތޯ؟ މިއަދު ޑޮލަރުގެ ވާހަކަދައްކަން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަކަށް އެހާ ފަސޭހައެއް ނުވާނެ. ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އަނިޔާ، އޮޅުވައިލުން، ނިކަމެތިކަން މި ޤައުމަށް ކުރިމަތިކުރި ބަޔަކީ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ. ކީއްވެތޯ؟ އެއީ ދޮގާއި، މަކަރާއި ހީލަތް ހަދައިގެން ވެސް ވެރިކަމާ ހަމައަށް އަންނަން، ވެރިކަމަށް އައުމަށްފަހުގައި މަސައްކަތް މި ކުރަނީ އެ މީހުންނާ އެއްކޮށް މަސައްކަތްކުރި މީހުންގެ ވަޒީފާތައް ދިނުމާއި، ގޯތިތައް ދިނުމާއި، ފްލެޓު ދިނުމާއި، ފަޅުރަށް ދިނުމާއި ވިޔަފާރި ދިނުމާ. މި ކަންކަމަކީ މިއީ އޮޅޭނެ ކަމެއް ނޫން. އައްޑުއަތޮޅު ހުޅުދޫ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެނގޭނެ އެ ރަށުން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގެ ސަރުކާރުގައި ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރި މީހުން. މި ސަރުކާރުން މިއަދާ ހަމައަށް ދިޔަ އިރު އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ޓަކައި މަސައްކަތްކުރި މީހުން ތިބީ ކޮން ހިސާބެއްގައިކަން، ޑިރެކްޓަރުންނަށް އެ ތިބީ. ތަންތަނުގެ އިސްވެރިންނަށް އެ ތިބީ. އެކަން ނުކޮށްގެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ މީހުން އެބަ ޝަކުވާކުރެއޭ. މިއަދު ވެސް އެބަ ޝަކުވާކުރޭ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަކަށް މިއަދުގެ ސަރުކާރުން ފިނޭންސް މިނިސްޓަރަކަށް ނުބެހެއްޓޭނެ އަމީރު. ނުބެހެއްޓޭނެ. އެއީ މި މީހުން މި ގަރާރު ލައިގެން މި ދައްކާ ވާހަކައަކީ. ވަޒީރުކަން ކިހިނެއްތޯ އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ދޭނީ. ކުންފުނިތަކުގެ އެމް.ޑީކަން
ކިހިނެއްތޯ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ މީހުންނަށް ދޭނީ. އެ މީހުންނާ ހަވާލުކުރި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން މިދިޔަ ފަސް އަހަރު. ޤައުމު ދިޔައީ ފަހަތަށް. އަޑިއަށް ދިޔައީ. ވަތަށް ދިޔައީ. އެހެންވީމާ، މިއަދުގެ ސަރުކާރު އައިސް ސަރުކާރު ހަމަމަގަށް އަޅުވައި ސަރުކާރު ކުރިއަށް މި ގެންދަނީ. މިކަމާ ހިތްހަމަނުޖެހިގެން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ މީހުން ކިތަންމެވަރަކަށް ގަރާރު ލިޔަސް، ކިތަންމެ ވާހަކައެއް ދެއްކިޔަސް މިކަން ގަބޫލުކުރާނެ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތަކު ނެތް. ނިމިދިޔަ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީ ސަރުކާރުން އައްޑުއަތޮޅު ހުޅުދޫ އިންޖީނުގެ ހަވާލުކޮށްފައި ހުރި ބޭފުޅާ ވަކިކޮށް ނަގައި އެއްލައިލީ މަގުމައްޗަށް. މިއަދު، މިއަދު ކާކުތޯ، އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރި ކާކުތޯ؟ އެހެންވީމާ، ގަރާރެއް ލައިގެން ވާހަކަދެއްކިޔަސް އަދި ޕޯޑިއަމަކަށް އަރައި ވާހަކަދެއްކިޔަސް ހުޅުދޫގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެނގޭނެ ހުޅުދޫއިން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ނިސްބަތްވާ އެކަކު ވެސް ނުކަނޑާކަން. އެއީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ސިޔާސަތެއް ނޫންކަން ވަޒީފާއިން މީހުން ކެނޑުމަކީ. އެހެންނަމަވެސް، ގަބޫލުކުރަންޖެހޭ ޙަޤީޤަތަކީ އައްޑުއަތޮޅު ހުޅުދޫ މީދޫގެ ވާހަކަ އަޅުގަނޑު ދައްކަން އެބަ ޖެހޭ. އިންޖީނުގެއެއް އަޅަން ރަށުގައި ތިބިއްޔާ ތިބި ހުރިހާ އެންމެން ވަޒީފާއަށް ނަގާފައި 18 ހާސް، 19 ހާސް، 20 ހާސް ރުފިޔާ ދީފައި، ކޮއްތު ފައިސާ ދީފައި، ކައްކަން ބަޔަކު ލާފަ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ބައްލަވާ، 5 އަހަރު ނިމިގެންދިޔަ އިރު އިންޖީނުގެ ސައިލެންސަރު އައީ، ވަށާ ފާރެއް ނުރޭނުނު އިންޖީނުގޭގެ. އެއީ ކީއްވެތޯ؟ އޭރު އިންޖީނުގެއާ ހަވާލުވެ ފެނަކައިގެ އެމް.ޑީގެ ކޮއްކޮއަށް އެ ޕްރޮޖެކްޓު ދިނީ 158 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ. އަދިވެސް އެ ތިބީ އެ މީހުން ނުކަނޑާ. ކުރާނެ މަސައްކަތެއް ވެސް ނެތް. އަދިވެސް މި ސަރުކާރުން ނުކަނޑައޭ. އަޅުގަނޑު ފޮނުވައިފީމޭ. އަޅުގަނޑު އެ ވާހަކަދައްކައިފީމޭ. ވެގެން އުޅޭ ގޮތަކީ ރަނގަޅަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރާ މީހުންނަށް ކުރިއެރުމެއް ނުލިބޭ އެ މީހުން ތިބިހާ ހިނދަކު. އެއްވެސް މަސައްކަތެއް އޮތީއެއް ނޫން. އެކަމަކު މި ބޭފުޅުން މި ބުނަނީ ގޭގައި ތިބެގެން އިނގިލި ޖަހައޭ. މުސާރަ ލިބެއޭ. އަނެއްކާ މިއަދު މި ބުނީ ކަނޑަނީއޭ. އެހެންވީމާ، މިއީ މިއަދު ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އޮޅޭނެ ވާހަކައެއް ނޫން. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އަތުގައި މި އޮތީ އިނގޭތޯ މިދިޔަ؛ ވަގުތުކޮޅެއް ދެއްވުން އެދެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ޕާޓީއަށް ވަގުތު އޮތިއްޔާމު. މިދިޔަ ސަރުކާރުގައި އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ޕާޓީ އޮފީހުގައި އޮންނާނެ ބޮޑު ދަފުތަރެއް. ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިވާ ކޮންމެ މީހަކު ކޮންމެ ރަށަކުން އައިސް ޕާޓީގެ އެ ދަފުތަރުގައި ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިވި ދުވަހާއި، ތާރީޚާއި، ކަނޑައިލި ސަބަބާއި، ކަނޑައިލި ގޮތާ މި އޮތީ ލިސްޓު. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަކީ މިއީ ހިސާބު އަކުރުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ރައީސް ވިދާޅުވާހެން، ހިސާބުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ނަތީޖާ ނެރެދޭނީ. ހިސާބުން ނަތީޖާ ނެރެދޭނީ. 2 އަހަރާއި 8 މަސްދުވަސްވީ އިރު 541 ޕްރޮޖެކްޓު މިހާރު ނިންމާފައި 1600 ޕްރޮޖެކްޓު މި ދަނީ ކުރިއަށް. ބައްލަވާ! މިދިޔަ 5 އަހަރު، 2 އަހަރާއި ބައިގައި އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިހަކަށްދުވަހު މި ވިދާޅުވި ފަދައިން ކޮން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓެއްތޯ ނިމުނީ؟ ކޮން ކަމެއްތޯ ކުރެވުނީ؟ އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަކީ ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅަށް އިދިކޮޅުގައި 5 އަހަރު ހޭދަކުރި އިރު ވެސް ޕާޓީ އޮފީސް އޭގެ ރަނގަޅު ގޮތުގައި ހިންގައި، ޕާޓީ އޮފީހުގައި ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިވާ މީހުން ވެސް، ހައްޔަރުވި މީހުންގެ އަދަދު ވެސް ހުންނާނެ. މިދިޔަ 5 އަހަރުގައި މި ބޭފުޅުންގެ އަނިޔާވެރިކަމުން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ޖަލަށް ގެންގޮސް މަގުމަތީގެ ހަރަކާތްތަކުގައި
ހައްޔަރުކުރި މީހުންގެ އަދަދު ވެސް، ހައްޔަރުކުރި ފަހަރު ވެސް ހުންނާނެ. 85 ފަހަރު އެބަ ހުރި އެކަކު ޖަލަށް ލާފަ. 75 ފަހަރު. އެކަމަކު އެ މީހުންނެއް ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ވަޒީފާއެއް ނުދެމޭ ކޮންމެހެން 85 ފަހަރު ޖަލަށް ދިޔައޭ ކިޔާފަ. އެހެންވީމާ، ސަބަބަކީ މި ބޭފުޅުން ބޭނުންފުޅު މިވަނީ މިއަދު އެއްކަލަ ބުނާހެން އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ސަރުކާރު ރައްޔިތުންނާ ޖައްސަން. ރައްޔިތުން ހިތްނުތަނަސްކޮށް، ރައްޔިތުންގެ ތެރޭގައި މި ބުނާ ގޮތަށް ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އޮޅުވާލައިގެން އިހަކަށް ރޭ ބޭއްވިއެއް ނޫންތޯ ޑޮލަރާ ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ވެސް ބޮޑުސިންގާ، މާސިންގާ އެއްޗެއް. ކޮން ބައެއްތޯ ތިބީ؟ އޭރު މި ޑޮލަރު ކުޑަކުރަން ތިބި މީހުންނޭ ތިބީ. މަޖިލީހުންނާއި ފިނޭންސް މިނިސްޓްރީންނޭ ތިބީ. އަރާފައި މި ބުނަނީ 800 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ފަހަތުން ދުވަނިއްޔޯ ޑޮލަރު. ޑޮލަރުގެ މައްސަލަ ހަލާކު، މި ޤައުމުގެ އިޤުތިޞާދު ހަލާކުކޮށްލީ އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީން. އަހަރަކު 300 މިލިއަން ރުފިޔާ ފައިދާއަށް ވަދެވަދެ ހުރެ އެމް.އޭ.ސީ.އެލް، މާލެ އެއަރޕޯޓު، ދިވެހިންގެ އެއަރޕޯޓު ބޭރުގެ ބަޔަކަށް 78 މިލިއަން ޑޮލަރަށޭ ކިޔާފައި ވިއްކައިލާފައި ޖީބަށް އަޅައިލީ 25 މިލިއަން ޑޮލަރު. އެ ހިސާބުން ރާއްޖޭގެ އިޤުތިޞާދު ދިޔައީ. ފެން ކުންފުނި ވިއްކާލީ. ދިރާގު ވިއްކާލީ. މިއީ އޮޅޭނެ އެއްޗެއް ނޫން. މިއީ މި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ކުރިމަތީގައި ހިނގައިދިޔަ ކަންތައްތައް. އެހެންވީމާ، މިއަދު އަރާ ތިމަންނަމެން ޑޮލަރު ފަހަތުންނޭ، ޑޮލަރޭ، ޑޮލަރު މަތިވަނިއްޔޭ، އިޤުތިޞާދޭ. މި ބޭފުޅުންގެ ސަބަބުން ޑޮލަރު މަތިވީ. އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ވެރިކަމާ ހަވާލުވެގެން މިއަދާ ހަމައަށް ލިބުނު ފައިސާއިން ކުރި ކަންތައް އެ އޮތީ ފެންނަން. ދިވެހި ދައުލަތް ސަލާމަތްކުރީ. ދިވެހި ދައުލަތަށް، ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ބޭރަށް ދެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހެދީ. ބޭސްފަރުވާއަށް ދެވޭނެ ގޮތް ހެދީ. ބޭސް އެތެރެނުވެގެން ލަސްވީ ކީއްވެތޯ؟ އެ ވާހަކަ ތަކުރާރުކޮށް ނެތިން. މިއީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެން އަބަދު ވެސް ދައްކާ ވާހަކަ. މި ވާހަކަދައްކަންޖެހެނީ، ކުރީ ސަރުކާރުގެ ވާހަކަދައްކަންޖެހެނީ މިއަދު އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ހަވާލުވެގެން ކުރިއަށްދާ އިރު ކުރިއަށް ބޮޑަށް ކަނޑައިގެން ގޮސް ރައްޔިތުންނާ ހަމައަށް މީގެ އަސްލު ޙަޤީޤީ މަންފާ ނުވަތަ މި ޙަޤީޤީ ކުރިއެރުން ނުލިބިގެން މި އުޅެނީ މި ބޭފުޅުން ޤައުމު ހިންގާފައި މި އޮތީކީ ޤައުމު ހިންގާ އުސޫލަކުން ނޫން. މުޅިން އެހެން ގޮތަކަށް. މޭޒު ދަށުން ހިންގީ. މައްޗަކުން ނޫން. އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ސަރުކާރު މި ހިންގަނީ މަތިން. މަތިން ފެންނަ ގޮތަށް. ދެފުށްފެންނަ ކީއްކުރަން، ހަތަރު ފުށް ވެސް އެބަ ފެނޭ. ވަށައިޖެހޭ ގޮތަށް މި ދަނީ. ކޮންމެ ދިމާލަކުން ދިޔަސް ވަދެވޭނެ ސަރުކާރުގެ ކޮންމެވެސް އޮފީހަކަށް. މަޢުލޫމާތު ބަރާބަރަށް ދޭ. އެއްވެސް މައްސަލައެއް ދިމަލެއްނުވޭ. އެހެންވީމާ، އެކި ބޭބޭފުޅުން އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގައި، ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި މިއަދު އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީއަށް ދިމާވެގެން އުޅޭ މައްސަލައަކީ ވެރިކަމަށް އަންނަން އެންމެން ވެސް ބޭނުންވެފައި ތިބީ. އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިޙް އަދިވެސް ބޭނުން އެބަ ވޭ. ރައީސް ނަޝީދު ވެސް ބޭނުން އެބަ ވޭ. ބޭނުން ނޫނޭ ކިޔައިގެން ހުންނަނީ ކުރިމައްޗަށް ބަޔަކު ނެރެގެން. ދެން ޑރ. ޝަމްހީދު ވެސް ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ބޭނުންވެގެން މިދިޔަ ބޮޑު ޓީމެއް ހައްދަވާފައި މުޅި ރާއްޖޭގައި ދަތުރުކުރެއްވި. ވަރަށް ރަނގަޅު އެ މަނިކުފާނު. މަޖިލީހުގައި ތިއްބެވި މެންބަރުންނާ އެއްކޮށް. ރަނގަޅު! އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ތާއީދުކުރަން މަޖިލިސް މެންބަރަކަށްވީތީ އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ އަޚެއް ވީމާ، އެ ބޭފުޅާއަށް އަޅުގަނޑު
ތާއީދުކުރަން ހަމަ ގައިމު ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑު ދަންނަ ރައްޓެއްސަކަށްވާތީވެ. އެހެންނަމަވެސް، އެއީ ނޫން ދެއްތޯ، ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން ބައްލަވާނެ މި ހުރިހާ ކަމެއް. ވަރަށް ގާތުން ބައްލަވާނެ ހުރިހާ ކަމެއް. ބައްލަވާފައި ނޫނީ މި ނިންމުން ނުނިންމާނެ. ކިތަންމެ ވަރަކަށް ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ދޮގާއި މަކަރާއި ހީލަތުން ރައްޔިތުން އޮޅުވައިލަން މަސައްކަތްކުރެވިދާނެ. ވާހަކަދެއްކިދާނެ. ވަޒީފާއިން ވަތްކެއްނުކުރާނެ މި ސަރުކާރަކުން. ކުންފުންޏަކުން އެ ކުންފުނީގެ ކަންކަން އިންތިޒާމުކޮށް ބެލެހެއްޓުމަކީ އެ ކުންފުންޏަށް ލާޒިމުކުރާ ކަމެއް. އެ ކުންފުނީގެ އެމް.ޑީއަކު ޒިންމާވާންޖެހޭނެ އެކަމަކަށް. ސަރުކާރުން ކުރާ ކަމެއް ނޫން ކުންފުންޏަކުން މީހުން ވަޒީފާއަށް ނެގުން، ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރުމަކީ. މިއީ ވެސް އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ގަބޫލުކުރަންޖެހޭ ޙަޤީޤަތެއް. ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ކިހިނެއްތޯ ޒިންމާ ނަންގަވާނީ؟ ކުންފުންޏެއްގެ ވެރިޔެއް އެބަ ހުރި ލިޔެކިޔުމުން ހަވާލުވެގެން ރަސްމީކޮށް އެ ޒިންމާ ނަންގަވައިގެން. އެ ބޭފުޅާގެ ޒިންމާއެއް ކުންފުނި އެ އޮންނަ އުސޫލެއްގެ ތެރެއިން ހަމަމަގަށް އަޅުވައި ހިންގުން. ފައިދާވާ ކުންފުންޏެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި މަސައްކަތްކޮށް ނެރެދިނުން. އެއީ ޤައުމުގެ ޙައްޤުގައި، ރައްޔިތުންގެ ޙައްޤުގައި އޭނައާ އެ މަތިކުރެވޭ އަމާނާތް އޭގެ އެންމެ ރަނގަޅު ގޮތުގައި ކުރިއަށްގެންދަން އޭނައަށް މަޖުބޫރުވާނެ. އެހެން ވެއްޖެއްޔާމު އެ ކުންފުނީގެ މުވައްޒަފުން އިތުރުކުރުމާއި މަދުކުރުމަކީ އޭނާގެ ޒިންމާއެއް. ހަމައެކަނި އޭނަ ނުޖެހޭނެ އިންޖީނެއް ގެންނާކަށް. ކޭބަލެއް ގެންނާކަށް. އެއީއެއް ނޫން އޭނަގެ ޒިންމާއަކީ. ކަރަންޓު ދިނުމެއް ނޫން. ކަރަންޓު ދިނުމަށް ޓަކައި ބޭނުންވާ ވަސީލަތްތައް ހޯދުމާއި އެކަން އޭގެ އެންމެ ފުރިހަމަ ގޮތުގައި ގެންދިއުމަކީ އޭނަގެ އެންމެ ބޮޑު ޒިންމާއެއް. ތަން ހިންގުން. އެހެންވީމާ، ތަން ހިންގުމަށް ޓަކައި ތަނަށް ބޭނުންވާ މުވައްޒަފުން ހޯދުމާއި އަދި އެއަށްވުރެ އިތުރަށް ހުރި މުވައްޒަފުންތައް އެކި ގޮތްގޮތަށް ހަމަމަގަށް އެޅުވުމަކީ އޭނާގެ ޒިންމާއެއް. އެއީ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ކުރައްވާ ކަމެއް ނޫން. ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ޒިންމާއެއް ނޫން. ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އޮޅުވައިލަން ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިސްތަށިފުޅުގައި މީހަކު ވަޒީފާއިން ވަކިކުރީމާ، މީހަކު ވަޒީފާއަށް ވެއްދީމާ. ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީގެ 115 ވަނަ މާއްދާއިން ލިބިގެންވާ ބާރެއްގެ ދަށުން އެ މަނިކުފާނު އައްޔަންކުރާ ސިޔާސީ މަގާމަކީ އެ މަގާމުތަކުގައި އައްޔަންކުރައްވާ ބޭފުޅުން ބައްލަވަންވީ އިތުރުތޯ، މަދުތޯ. އެ އިޚުތިޔާރު އޮންނާނެ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާއަށް ލިބިގެން. ޤާނޫނުއަސާސީން އަޅުގަނޑުމެން ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުން އޮންނާނެ މަތިކޮށްފައި އެ ބާރުވެރިކަން. އެހެންވީމާ، އެއްވެސް ހާލެއްގައި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އޮޅުވައިލުމަށް ޓަކައި މި ތަނަށް ގަރާރު ހުށަހަޅައިގެން، މުޅިން އެހެން ގޮތަކަށް ވެރިކަން ހޯދުމުގެ މަކަރާއި ހީލަތް ޖަހައިގެން ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އޮޅުވާލައި ދޮގު ހަދައިގެން މިއަދަކު ވެރިކަމެއް އަތެއް ނުވާނެ. ވެރިކަން އަތުލާން ބޭނުން ކަމަށް ވެއްޖެއްޔާ، އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީން ވެރިކަން ހޯދަން ބޭނުން ކަމަށް ވަންޏާ އަދިވެސް ޖެހޭނީ އިޞްލާޙުވާން. އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގެ ނަން ފޮހެލަންވީ. އެހެން ނަމެއްގައި އަންނަންވީ. އެކަމަކު އެމް.ޑީ.ޕީގައި މި ތިއްބެވި ވެރިން އެހެން ނަމެއްގައި ވެސް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެނގިލައްވާނެ އެ ބޭފުޅުން އިތުރުފުޅު ހައްދަވާނެކަން. އެ ބޭފުޅުންނަކީ މަކަރާއި ހީލަތް މީގެ ކުރީގައި ވެސް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ޓަކައި ވަރަށް
ބޮޑެތި، ވަރަށް ބޮޑެތި ދޮގުހައްދަވާފައި ތިއްބެވި ބޭފުޅުންކަން އެނގިލައްވާނެ. މުޅިން އާ މޫނުތައް އަންނަންވީ. މުޅިން އާ ޕާޓީއެއް ހަދައިގެން މުޅިން އާ ގޮތަކަށް އައިސްގެން ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ތެދުވެރިކަމާއި އިޚުލާސްތެރިކަމާ އެއްކޮށް ޚިދުމަތްކުރުމަށް ވަކާލާތުކޮށް އެ ޔަގީންކަން އުފައްދަންވީ. މިހާރު މި އޮތް ގޮތަކަށް އަދި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނެއް އެ ބޭފުޅުންނަކަށް ވެރިކަމެއް ހަވާލެއްނުކުރައްވާނެ. ޝުކުރިއްޔާ ދެއްވި ފުރުޞަތަށް ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް.
speeches.en:
Thank you, Honourable Speaker. I too sought the opportunity to speak on this resolution submitted by the Honourable Member for Kendhoo constituency, Mauroof Zakir, because previously in this Majlis, in the last session that was held, they spoke, and today too what they generally talk about is this government not appointing people to jobs. About not appointing large numbers of the people living on the islands to jobs. Today, again, what has been submitted and is going forward is about dismissing people from jobs. So, first of all, I have to believe that the MDP has not come to this country for the first time. It is not for the first time that they are working to address the people of this country and gain power. The Maldivian people will not be confused about this. When the MDP is mentioned, the people will now be afraid. They will run backwards. That is because of what they said: the very first time they came to power, when they took over the government in 2008, how did they do things? The dollar is also being talked about. At what level was the price of the dollar then? When President Nasheed's two and a half years of government ended, at what level was the dollar? Today it will not be that easy for the MDP to talk about the dollar. In reality, the party that brought oppression, deception and destitution upon the Maldivian people and this country is the MDP. Why? Because they come to power even through lies, deceit and trickery, and after coming to power the work they do is giving jobs, giving housing plots, giving flats, giving uninhabited islands and giving business to the people who worked with them. These are not things anyone can be confused about. The people of Hulhudhoo in Addu Atoll will know the people from that island who were dismissed from jobs under the MDP government. Under this government, up to today, look at where the people who worked for the MDP are: they are directors. They are heads of institutions. Our people complain that this was not done. Even today they complain. We cannot appoint Ameer as Finance Minister in today's government. Cannot appoint him. That is what these people are saying by bringing this resolution. How would we give ministerial posts? How would we give the MD posts of companies

to MDP people? The Maldivian people entrusted the country to them for the past five years. The country went backwards. It went to the bottom. It fell into a pit. So, today's government has come, put the government on the right track and is taking the government forward. Unhappy with this, however many resolutions MDP people write and however much they talk, there is no Maldivian citizen who will accept this. The past MDP government removed the person who was in charge of the Hulhudhoo powerhouse in Addu Atoll and threw him out onto the street. Today, today who is it, who is it that worked in the MDP? So, even if they talk by bringing a resolution and even if they climb onto a podium and talk, the people of Hulhudhoo will know that not a single person from Hulhudhoo affiliated with the MDP is being cut. That dismissing people from jobs is not our policy. However, the truth that has to be accepted is that I must speak about Hulhudhoo-Meedhoo in Addu Atoll. To build a powerhouse, they took everyone on the island into employment, gave them 18 thousand, 19 thousand, 20 thousand rufiyaa, gave them kotthu money, and put people on to cook. Honourable Speaker, look, when 5 years had ended, the powerhouse silencer arrived, for a powerhouse that did not even have a surrounding wall built. Why is that? At that time, upon taking charge of the powerhouse, the project was given to the younger sibling of FENAKA's MD for 158 million rufiyaa. Those people are still there, not cut. There is no work for them to do either. They say this government still does not cut them. They say, 'I have sent it. I have talked about it.' What is happening is that people who work well do not get advancement as long as those people remain. There is no work at all. But these people are saying that they stay at home, press their finger [on the attendance machine] and get a salary. And again today they are saying they are being cut. So, this is not something the people will be confused about today. What we have in our hands, you know, the past; I request a little time if our party has time. In the past government there was a big register in our party office. Every person dismissed from a job came from every island, and in that party register there is the list with the day they were dismissed, the date, the reason they were cut and the way they were cut. We, as our President says, in figures, we will deliver results with figures. Deliver results with figures. In 2 years and 8 months, 541 projects have now been completed and 1600 projects are under way. Look! In the past 5 years, in 2 and a half years, as our President said the other day, which project was completed? What was done? So, even when we spent 5 years in the opposition, we ran the party office very well, properly, and in the party office there will be the people dismissed from jobs and the number of those arrested. In the past 5 years, because of these people's oppression, we were taken to jail, in street activities

the number of people arrested and the number of times they were arrested will be there. There is one person who was jailed 85 times. 75 times. But we cannot give those people jobs just because they say they went to jail 85 times. So, the reason is that what these people want today, as one of them said, is to make our government clash with the people. Discouraging the people, misleading the people among the people in the way they say: didn't they hold something big and grand last night regarding the dollar too? Who were they? At that time they were the ones who were there to bring the dollar down. They were in the Majlis and in the Finance Ministry. They come up and say the dollar is running after 800 million rufiyaa [unclear]. The dollar problem, the ruin; the MDP ruined this country's economy. MACL, the Malé airport, the Maldivians' own airport, which was bringing in 300 million rufiyaa of profit a year, was sold to a foreign party, saying it was for 78 million dollars, and 25 million dollars were put into pockets. That is how the Maldivian economy went. They sold the water company. They sold Dhiraagu. This is not something to be confused about. These are things that happened in front of the Maldivian people. So, today they come up saying 'we are after the dollar, the dollar, the dollar is rising, the economy'. It is because of these people that the dollar rose. What has been done with the money received since our President took office up to today is there to be seen. He saved the Maldivian state. He made it possible for the Maldivian state, for the people, to go abroad. Made it possible to go for medical treatment. Why was there a delay because medicines were not imported? I will not repeat that. This is something we always talk about. The reason we have to talk about this, have to talk about the previous government, is that today, as we take charge and move forward, cutting far ahead, the real benefit or the real progress of this does not reach the people because these people ran the country not by the principles of running a country. In a completely different way. They ran it under the table. Not from above. We run the government from above. In a way that can be seen from above. Why only two sides visible, all four sides can be seen. It goes round so it can be seen all around. Whichever direction you go, you can enter some government office. Information is given properly. No problem at all arises. So, various people in the MDP; in reality, the problem facing the MDP today is that everyone wants to come to power. Ibrahim Mohamed Solih still wants it. President Nasheed also wants it. They pretend not to want it by putting someone else forward. Then Dr. Shamheed also wanted it very much and formed a big team and travelled across the whole of the Maldives. Very good of him. Together with the members who were in the Majlis. Good! We support him because he is a Majlis member, as he is our brother, I

support him, certainly, because he is a friend I know. However, that is not it, right; the Maldivian people will look at all these things. They will look very closely at everything. This decision will not be made without looking. However much we may try to mislead the people with lies, deceit and trickery. We may talk. This government will not dismiss anyone from jobs. Managing and overseeing a company's affairs is something that is obligatory on that company. The MD of that company must be responsible for that. A company hiring people and dismissing people from jobs is not something the government does. This too is a truth we have to accept. How would the President take responsibility? There is a head of the company who has taken charge in writing and has formally assumed that responsibility. That person's responsibility is to run the company on the right track within the principles under which it operates. To work and make it a profitable company. He will be obliged to carry out, in the best way, the trust placed upon him for the sake of the nation and the people. If so, increasing and decreasing the company's employees is his responsibility. He does not only have to bring an engine. To bring a cable. That is not his responsibility. It is not providing electricity. Obtaining the resources needed to provide electricity and carrying it out in the most complete way is his greatest responsibility. Running the place. So, finding the staff the place needs to run and putting the excess staff on the right track in various ways is his responsibility. That is not something the President does. It is not the President's responsibility. To mislead the people, it is put on the President's head when someone is dismissed from a job, when someone is hired. The political posts the President appoints under the power granted by Article 115 of the Constitution: whether the people appointed to those posts should be more or fewer, that discretion lies with the President. We, the Maldivian people, have conferred that power through the Constitution. So, under no circumstances will anyone gain power today by submitting resolutions here to mislead the Maldivian people, by using deceit and trickery to gain power in a completely different way, by misleading the people and lying. If they want to seize power, if the MDP wants to gain power, they still have to reform. They should erase the MDP's name. They should come under another name. But even under another name, the Maldivian people will know that the leaders now in the MDP have only grown bigger [unclear]. Those people previously, with deceit and trickery, told the Maldivian people very

big, very big lies; the Maldivian people will know they are the ones who told them. Entirely new faces should come. They should form an entirely new party, come in an entirely new way, advocate serving the Maldivian people with honesty and sincerity, and create that confidence. As things stand now, the Maldivian people will not hand power to those people. Thank you very much for the opportunity given.

speeches.name: Ahmed Saleem
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު. ދެން ފުރުޞަތު މި އަރުވަނީ ތޮއްޑޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޙުސައިން ސަމީރަށް.
speeches.en: Thank you, Honourable Member. Next, I give the floor to the Honourable Member for Thoddoo constituency, Hussain Sameer.
